meters.label: Packages rebuilt by a change to the shared helper

frames.narration: A product is split into 7 packages: web, orders, billing, customers, notifications, reports and utils. Arrows are dependencies, and a change to a package forces everything above it to rebuild and retest.
utils holds unrelated helpers. Five packages use it and it is changed 12 times a quarter, so each change rebuilds and retests all 7 of 7 packages. 241 package builds a quarter come from this graph.
A cycle has crept in: orders uses billing, billing uses customers, customers uses orders, and utils uses customers too. These 4 packages cannot be built, tested or released alone.

The arrows also point the wrong way. utils looks stable, with instability 16 because 5 packages use it, but it depends on customers at 40: a package depending on something less stable. The graph has 2 such violations.

Split utils into money (1 change a quarter) and text (2), and make customers depend on nothing above it. No cycles, no violations, and builds per quarter fall from 241 to 117. The helper everyone uses now almost never changes.

Over-split: an api and an impl package for everything gives 13 packages. A change to an implementation rebuilds 2 of 13, but a feature that adds a customer field edits 5 packages instead of 3, and builds per quarter are 113 against 117. More release units, little gained.
Point dependencies from changing packages toward steady ones, keep the graph acyclic, keep the shared base small and rarely changed, and split packages by reason to change rather than by habit.
